context:
Sequence is deliberate and dependency-aware:
- w1-w3 (Critical) ship first, individually. Each is a contract bug
  that breaks production and needs no shared infrastructure.
- w4-w5 (shared-helper foundation) ship next. They are the leverage
  that makes w8/w11 mechanical instead of bespoke per-adapter.
- w6 (P11 visibility cluster) and w7 (N1 throughput inflation) are
  independent of the foundation work — can ship in parallel with w4/w5.
- w8/w9/w10 (modularity-drift extractions) ship after w4/w5.
- w11/w22/w23/w12 (per-adapter regex fixes) ship after w5 in bounded
  adapter-family slices.
- w13/w14 are independent one-liners.
- w15 (ABC test) ships after w3 and gates future regressions.
- w16/w17/w24/w25/w18/w19/w26/w20 are cleanup; ship last.

Reference the canonical fixes already in the repo:
- benchbox/platforms/_spark_helpers.py for balanced-paren walker,
  SparkLikeAdapterMixin, "Import discipline" docstring block
- benchbox/platforms/{spark,lakesail,velox}.py for the lambda-capture
  pattern (w10-style), the on_pre_loop hook wiring, the
  --platform-option error message rewrite (P3 canonical fix)
- docker/velox/docker-compose.yml for the canonical tmpfs pattern
  that w20 should mirror

Grep before each work unit:
  git diff 73f3a582e -- <file>     # confirm file hasn't drifted from audit baseline
  grep -n '<exact snippet>' <file> # confirm line numbers
Audit lines were captured at 73f3a582e; subsequent commits may shift them.
description:
A 13-pattern defect audit across 30 platform adapters (excluding the
already-fixed spark/lakesail/velox triple), shared helpers in
benchbox/platforms/base/, cloud_shared.py, presto_trino_utils.py,
questdb_rewriter.py, datafusion_*.py rewriters, benchbox/sql_compat/,
and all docker/*/ surfaced 33 actionable findings: 3 Critical, 22 Required,
and 8 Nit/Consider. Those findings span the original 13-pattern catalogue
plus 4 newly-named patterns (P14 stale-flag-coexistence,
P15 reference-before-assignment, N1 COUNT(*) throughput inflation,
N2 ABC contract divergence).

The audit ran on commit 73f3a582e (post velox/lakesail/spark fixes for
W8/W9/W10). The canonical fixes for patterns 1-13 already exist in
benchbox/platforms/_spark_helpers.py (`_strip_balanced_paren_constraints`,
the "import discipline" docstring block, the SparkLikeAdapterMixin)
and benchbox/platforms/{spark,lakesail,velox}.py — implementers should
port those patterns rather than reinvent.

Work units are sequenced by blast radius and dependency order: Critical
contract bugs first, then shared-helper drift (highest leverage), then
destructive-op visibility, then the silent-throughput bug, then
modularity-drift extractions, then the long tail of P1/P2 regex bugs
in individual adapters.

Audit report and pattern catalogue are in conversation context (not
committed). This TODO is intended to be self-contained enough to start
implementation, but every work unit must still confirm the cited snippet
against the current file before editing because line numbers were captured
at commit 73f3a582e.

anti_patterns.dont: 'fix' the deferred speculative items (FK column expressions, CTE column lists)
anti_patterns.why: they are guarded by 'speculative' for a reason. The audit explicitly downgraded them. Re-evaluate only when a real failing benchmark surfaces.

anti_patterns.dont: batch the 3 Critical fixes into a single PR
anti_patterns.why: each touches different test files and orthogonal failure modes; landing them separately keeps blast radius small if one regresses

anti_patterns.dont: change the PG adapter from_config signatures during w9
anti_patterns.why: only extract the duplicated body. Caller compatibility comes first.

anti_patterns.dont: delete questdb._strip_fk_constraints in w4 without first running questdb integration tests
anti_patterns.why: it carries inline-REFERENCES handling that the base helper does not yet have

anti_patterns.dont: promote questdb.py:476-480 pre-create DROP failures to logger.info in w6
anti_patterns.why: the audit specifically calls for `warning` (failed destructive intent), not info
without it, the next snowpark_connect-style divergence will land silently, and the C3 fix becomes wasted work the moment someone adds a new adapter

anti_patterns.dont: treat `_project/TODO/` or `_project/DONE/` as product-code scope during implementation
anti_patterns.why: TODO status moves, work-unit completion, and index regeneration are required by the workflow

deferrals.reason: Speculative — current TPC schemas don't use functional refs in column lists. Re-evaluate when a benchmark adds expressions inside REFERENCES col lists.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Speculative regex hardening explicitly deferred until a benchmark adds expression-based FK refs in column lists; no such benchmark exists yet.
deferrals.summary: P1 (Consider) — base/ddl_helpers.py:28,31 inline `[^)]*` in FK column-list regex

deferrals.reason: Speculative — bare-identifier-only CTE column lists are universal. Will be addressed when the rewriter migrates to SQLGlot AST per its own design philosophy.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Explicitly speculative; deferred to a future SQLGlot-AST migration of the rewriter that has not been scheduled.

deferrals.reason: Speculative — Fabric managed Spark runtime ships Iceberg JARs by default on supported runtime versions. Add probe only if a real failure surfaces.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Explicitly speculative: add fabric_spark Iceberg classpath probe only if a real failure surfaces. No failure reported.

deferrals.reason: Most cloud DW and embedded engines have no local docker dir; the questdb finding (w20) was the only one in the audited set.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] obsolete: Reason states cloud DW/embedded engines have no local docker dir; questdb was the only actual finding in the audited set — nothing left to audit.
deferrals.summary: Audit duckdb/sqlite/snowflake docker dirs for P5

work_units.notes:
timescaledb.py:378-393 — psycopg2 keeps the txn open after a failed
cursor.execute. Add `connection.rollback()` in the except branch
(mirror postgresql.py:440). Optional improvement: adopt the parent's
FK-strip retry path instead of replacing it.
Trigger: any benchmark whose first DDL stmt fails (extension-dependent
type, missing role) — every subsequent stmt then raises
InFailedSqlTransaction and warning-logs, so the whole schema silently
fails.
work_units.summary: C1 — Add per-statement rollback to timescaledb create_schema DDL loop

snowpark_connect.py:291,314,385 vs spark.py:590,632,663.
create_schema(self, schema_name=None) → must accept (benchmark, connection).
load_data(self, tables, source_dir, file_format=...) → must accept
(benchmark, connection, data_dir).
execute_query(self, query, **kwargs) → must accept (connection, query,
query_id, ...) and return the standard dict
{query_id, stream_id, status, execution_time_seconds, ...}.

the count includes pre-existing rows and silently inflates throughput
in published BenchmarkResults.

loop and assign once. Add a regression test that loads two files
into a non-empty table and asserts total_rows_loaded == sum of new
file row counts only.
work_units.summary: N1 — Fix ClickHouse Cloud COUNT(*) throughput inflation in S3/GCS load loops
